items.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
items.excerpt: Genie 4 introduces real-time interactive world simulation with native audio, advanced physics, natural human motion, and steering powered by Gemini models.
items.rationale: Primary-source release of a new real-time interactive world model, the biggest tool news for game prototyping this cycle.

items.title: Epic Games is updating its EULA to allow AI training
items.excerpt: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney casually states that the EULA for using Epic's engines will allow for training AI on the output.
items.rationale: A concrete licensing change: AI training on Unreal Engine and MetaHuman output becomes allowed, which matters to every UE developer.

items.title: AI video game wikis riddled with errors are taking over, and pushing real fans to the side
items.excerpt: LLM-powered wikis, often full of inaccurate or irrelevant information, are starting to take over, leaving fans sidelined and publishers playing whack-a-mole.
items.rationale: Fresh reported angle (LLM-generated fan wikis) that the section has not covered, with publishers responding.

items.title: Peter Molyneux believes 'it's almost impossible to code now without using AI'
items.excerpt: The father of the god game weighs in on AI use in the gaming industry
items.rationale: A veteran designer says outright that the industry is quietly using AI for code, a counterpoint to the anti-AI statements from studios.

items.title: Zero Escape Writer Is Pro-AI, Believes His New Studio's Game Wouldn't Have Been Canceled If He'd Used It To Cut Costs
items.excerpt: Kotaro Uchikoshi understands the resistance to AI, but feels it is necessary to cut costs and make games faster
items.rationale: A narrative-game auteur links a real cancelled project to AI cost economics, a concrete case from the Japanese side of the debate.
